observations: Front panel shows 'MAXI' branding, a power button, and three indicator LEDs for fault, battery, and AC power.
Rear panel features two UK-style three-pin sockets and two IEC C13 sockets.
A specification label is visible on the side/top of the unit.
The unit appears dusty and shows signs of use.

risks.risk: Internal batteries (24V system) may be dead or have very low capacity.
risks.proof: A video showing the UPS powering a significant load (e.g., a desktop PC or lamp) while unplugged from the wall for at least 5 minutes.
risks.if_unproven: as having dead batteries requiring replacement

risks.risk: The charging circuit or inverter may be faulty.
risks.proof: A video showing the unit turning on, charging (AC LED on), and switching to battery mode (Battery LED on) when the wall plug is pulled.

proof_requests: Video of the unit powered on and switching to battery mode under load.
Photo of the unit with the AC power disconnected while a device is plugged into it and running.
response.reason: The brand and model are clearly identified from the photos, allowing for a valuation based on its worst-case condition (dead batteries/non-functional).
